page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance configured with 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.3 GHz across 2 physical cores with 2 hyperthreads per core. It provides 26.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 6.5 GB per core. The processor features 45 MB of L3 cache alongside standard hardware instruction extensions including AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA. This instance type contains no bundled local NVMe or SSD storage and includes no discrete GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates legacy-tier computational throughput. Single-core and multi-core CPU testing via stress-ng yielded scores of 1109.89 and 2914.17 respectively, while Geekbench recorded a single-core score of 924.0 and a multi-core score of 2032.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks measured 162.39 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 25.86 GB/sec for large uncached read operations. Specialized synthetic tests show 2.75 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 2.82 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an architectural perspective, the n1-highmem-4 offers cost efficiency primarily for memory-bound workloads that do not demand high clock speeds or recent processor instructions like AVX-512 or AMX. Tradeoffs include lower single-threaded processing capacity and reliance on remote network storage. Consequently, the instance is suitable for small in-memory key-value stores, caching layers, web serving, and database environments requiring substantial RAM overhead relative to compute requirements.
